finalists.label: Kawasaki disease
finalists.why: It has the strongest for evidence, including fever and erythema on trunk and extremities after vaccination, high troponin levels, and total occlusion of the atrioventricular branch of the right coronary artery, with no against evidence.

finalists.label: Vasculitis
finalists.why: It has specific for evidence, including total occlusion of the atrioventricular branch of the right coronary artery and 90% stenotic lesions with coronary ectasia in the left circumflex artery, with no against evidence.

finalists.label: Acute coronary syndrome
finalists.why: It has strong for evidence, including high troponin levels, total occlusion of the atrioventricular branch of the right coronary artery, and 90% stenotic lesions with coronary ectasia in the left circumflex artery, with no against evidence.

frontier_selector.why: Kawasaki disease is chosen because it accounts for the most decisive findings in the vignette, including the temporal relationship between vaccination and symptom onset, and has no against evidence.
